paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita.) He is mentioned in [Shabbat 106b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.106b.9) on the law of one who catches locusts on Shabbat: he says that if they were coming in swarms he is exempt; so it is in [the Tosefta there, chapter 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Shabbat.13.4). He is likewise mentioned in [Yevamot 120a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.120a.14) and [Bava Metzia 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.27b.12): one may identify the deceased by testimony about a mole.[^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital text has the mole testimony at Yevamot 120a, with Rabbi Eliezer ben Mehavai, and Bava Metzia 27b, with Elazar. Hyman’s supplied Yevamot 102a and Bava Metzia 27a remain alongside those matching locations. שומא here is a mole, not an unspecified identifying sign; the Elazar/Eliezer distinction is retained.

The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=557&lang=en) gives both of the linked Bavli locations for the mole ruling. For the locust ruling, both [Shabbat](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.106b.9) and the [Tosefta](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Shabbat.13.4) specify that the exemption for swarming locusts applies even in the heat of the day.
